title: Ship the Run When the PO System Is Down
skill: Degraded-mode output under a failed dependency
scenario: It is 2:15 PM and the PO register is down. Without it, not one invoice can be three-way matched - you cannot confirm price or quantity against the order. The 3:00 PM run still has to ship. Shipping it well is a designed skill: pay nothing you cannot verify, hold the rest, put the outage in the run, and say who approved the safe posture.
inputLabel: Outage facts + the safe degraded posture
input:
Assembly rule for a degraded run: with the PO register unavailable, no invoice can be matched, so none may be paid. The run renders from stored artifacts, pays zero, holds every invoice that needs a match, and carries an Incident section. The AP Manager approves the pay-nothing posture; vendors are told payment moves to the next business day once the register is restored.

Outage facts: the PO register went down at 1:45 PM, detected at 1:50 PM, IT ticket INC-4471. Six invoices are in today's batch, all needing a match. Paid today: 0. Held: 6. Cutoff: 3:00 PM. Approved by the AP Manager at 2:30 PM. Run mode: degraded.
instructions: Open the payment batch and the PO register status on the shelf.
Fill the run summary: cutoff, invoices paid (0), invoices held (6).
Fill the Incident section from the outage facts: when it went down, when detected, the ticket id.
State the run mode (degraded) and who approved the pay-nothing posture and when.

validation.template:
# Beacon Payment Run - degraded (PO register outage)
Status: released without payments - the PO register is down, so no invoice could be three-way matched.

## Run summary
Date: day-1. Cutoff: {{cutoff}}. Invoices paid: {{paidCount}}. Invoices held: {{heldCount}}.

## Incident
The PO register went down at {{outageAt}}, detected {{detectedAt}} (ticket {{ticketId}}). Without the PO system the price and quantity legs cannot be verified, so every invoice needing a match is held.

## Posture
This run is marked {{runMode}}: paying an unverified invoice is the one mistake an outage must never cause. Approved by {{approvedBy}} at {{approvedAt}}. Vendors were notified that payment moves to the next business day once the PO register is restored.

copilotPrompt: Assemble a degraded payment run for a PO-register outage. Pay 0, hold 6, and fill the Incident section (down at 1:45 PM, detected 1:50 PM, ticket INC-4471). Mark the run degraded, approved by the AP Manager at 2:30 PM, cutoff 3:00 PM. Render payment-run.md from the template.
successMessage: Degraded run shipped. It pays nothing it cannot verify, carries its own outage, and names who approved the safe posture - honest beats fast on a broken afternoon.

intro.heading: Before you assemble: a failed dependency is a design problem

sections.title: You cannot match, so you cannot pay
sections.body: The three-way match needs the PO register to confirm price and quantity. With the register down, every leg is unverifiable. The safe posture is not to guess - it is to pay nothing that needs a match. An outage must never become the reason an unverified invoice got paid.

sections.title: The run carries its own incident
sections.body: A degraded run that looks normal is a lie by omission. This one puts the outage IN the deliverable: the reader sees the register failed, when, and the ticket, in the same glance as the zero paid. Failures surface where people actually look.

sections.title: Explain the empty run, do not just ship a blank
sections.body: A run that pays nothing with no explanation reads like a broken process. This one states the reason and names the AP Manager who approved paying nothing. An empty run, explained and approved, is a working control; an empty run, unexplained, is a fire drill.

sections.title: Held is not lost
sections.body: The six invoices are not rejected - they are held for the next business day once the register is back, and vendors are told. Degraded mode defers work safely instead of dropping it, so tomorrow's desk picks up exactly where this one paused.

takeaway.heading: Degraded run shipped
points: You shipped on time with a dead dependency and paid nothing you could not verify - the outage never became a payment mistake.
The run carries its own incident: the reader learns the register failed, when, and the ticket, without hunting through a separate log.
The empty run is explained and approved, not a silent blank, so a control working correctly does not read like a failure.
Held invoices are deferred to the next business day with vendors notified, so the work is paused safely rather than dropped.
The workflow can now produce a trustworthy run on exactly the afternoons a broken system used to turn into guesswork.
